preserved_analysis.failure_mode_definition: A failure mode where the action surface of an AI or agentic system is broader than the audit/report surface provided to the user, evaluator, regulator, or governance maintainer. The system may not be lying; the failure arises when its report compresses or omits material primitives such as objective interpretation, constraints applied, prohibited means considered, tool calls, failed attempts, fallback pathways, uncertainty states, evaluator-context cues, or user-impacting decisions. The result is an incomplete or misleading governance picture even when the task outcome appears complete.
preserved_analysis.failure_threshold: The threshold is met when a model or agentic system completes or attempts a task but its report omits material steps, assumptions, tool actions, failed paths, context changes, prohibitions, or uncertainty states that would reasonably affect auditability, consent, diagnosis, safety evaluation, repair routing, or user trust. The threshold is also met when public evaluation reports describe an outcome without preserving the operational primitive chain needed to distinguish error, task optimisation, instruction conflict, context variance, concealment, or deception.
